QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_17

question.text: Ms. Priya Shah (SIA) is designing the assessment methodology for Kiran Healthcare Pvt Ltd's cataract-surgery program. Of the following, which technique provides the STRONGEST causal inference about whether improved vision is due to the intervention?

answer.text: Pre-post comparison of the treated group only
Randomised Controlled Trial (RCT) with a randomly assigned control group
Narrative testimonials from ten satisfied beneficiaries

explanation.text: The Logic: RCT is the gold standard for causal inference: random assignment of treatment and control ensures the two groups are statistically equivalent except for the intervention, so post-intervention differences can be causally attributed to the intervention. The Trap: Pre-post without a control group cannot rule out secular trends. Self-assessment and testimonials are weakest — high selection bias, no counterfactual. Only RCT satisfies the counterfactual requirement rigorously. Cross-Exam Context: X-A/X-B IA and XV Research Analyst use RCT-evidence language for policy-research synthesis. XXIII expects the SIA to recognise RCT as the causal-inference gold standard. Assessor's Pro-Tip: RCTs are expensive and often infeasible for SEs — when RCT is impractical, escalate to quasi-experimental (DiD, propensity score matching) rather than dropping to pre-post, and disclose the design-choice rationale in your working papers.
